text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key part of clean code is following naming conventions. Good names for variables and functions should clearly explain what they do, so other people can understand your work quickly. It is also important to keep functions small and focused on one task. When functions are simple, it is easier to find and fix mistakes. Clean code is also easier to maintain, which means you can update it later without causing problems. In short, readable code saves time and helps teams work better together.
